# Story 50 — Ticket history reads as a sentence in order (Story: CRM-84)

## Prerequisites

- `TICKETS-1-API` (CRM-71) and `TICKETS-7-API` (CRM-83) must both be shipped so the history route is live. This story is **`web/` only** — no `api/` file changes.
- Familiarity with the shared UI primitives in `web/src/shared/ui/` and the `useRequest` four-state hook in `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts`.
- Read `.squad/plan-lessons.md` before starting — a plan that repeats a listed defect is rejected in review.

---

## Story Goal

Render the whole history of a single ticket, in chronological order, on the ticket detail area of the web app. Each entry reads as a full sentence in the reader's language (English or Arabic), built from resource strings — never from the raw verb or a database value. Timestamps are localised. The empty state announces "no history yet" (D-2). Paging is whatever the API returns; the screen adds none of its own (BR-4).

Explicit out of scope:

- **Filtering the history** — nothing asks for it.
- **A customer or article history** — this screen is a ticket's.
- **Any `api/` change** — the route ships with `TICKETS-7-API (CRM-83)`.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** no ticket-history screen exists in `web/`.
- **New behaviour:** a `TicketHistory` region on the ticket detail area fetches the API's history for a ticket, walks each entry, and renders one localised sentence per entry, in the same order the API returned them, using the API's paging cursor for "load more".

---

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Data hook: `useTicketHistory`

Create file: `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketHistory.ts`

- Signature: `useTicketHistory(ticketId: string) → { status, data, error, loadMore, reload }`.
- Uses `useRequest` from `web/src/shared/hooks`.
- Calls `request(\`/tickets/\${ticketId}/history\`)` (or whatever path CRM-83 exposes — confirm against `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.routes.js` before wiring). **Do not** add `/api/v1` — `base-url.ts:3` already prefixes it.
- Result shape mirrors the API envelope: `{ items: HistoryEntry[]; nextCursor: string | null }`. Never invent a page size on the client; pass through the cursor the API returns (BR-4).
- `HistoryEntry` type:
  ```ts
  export type HistoryEntry = {
    id: string;
    verb: string;              // e.g. 'ticket.status', 'ticket.assign'
    actor: { id: string; name: string } | null; // null when the system acted
    before: Record<string, string | null> | null;
    after: Record<string, string | null> | null;
    at: string;                // ISO-8601 UTC
  };
  ```
- On error, surface the API's error `code` unchanged so the page can look it up in `t.errors`.

### 2 — Sentence builder: verb → sentence with slots

Create file: `web/src/shared/i18n/history-sentence.ts`

- Export `formatHistorySentence(entry: HistoryEntry, t: Translations, formatValue: (field: string, value: string | null) => string): string`.
- Implementation:
  - Look up `t.tickets.history.sentences[entry.verb]` (a **whole sentence per language** with named placeholders, not a noun-verb-value glue).
  - Substitute placeholders using a tiny local function (regex on `{name}`). **No i18n library** — this lives next to the resource files, not on the page.
  - Slots available to every sentence: `{actor}`, `{fromStatus}`, `{toStatus}`, `{fromAssignee}`, `{toAssignee}`, `{fromCategory}`, `{toCategory}`, `{fromPriority}`, `{toPriority}`. Each slot value is itself translated (a status word from `t.tickets.status.*`, not `'pending'`).
  - Actor: when `entry.actor` is null, substitute `t.tickets.history.systemActor` (e.g. `"the system"` / equivalent Arabic). **Never invent a name.**
  - Unknown verb: when `t.tickets.history.sentences[entry.verb]` is missing, return `t.tickets.history.unknownVerb` filled with `{verb}` and `{actor}` — a legible fallback line, not a blank or a crash. History is append-only and future stories add verbs before sentences.
- Pure function; unit-tested in isolation (see Test Plan).

Why a whole sentence per language: English `"Sofia moved this from New to Open"` and its Arabic form differ in word order. Assembling by concatenation works in English and produces nonsense in Arabic. So each verb owns one string per language with placeholders.

### 3 — i18n resource keys (add to **both** `en.ts` and `ar.ts` in one edit)

File: `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`

Add under `tickets:`:

```ts
history: {
  heading: 'History',
  emptyTitle: 'No history yet',
  emptyBody: 'Nothing has happened on this ticket yet.',
  loadMore: 'Load more',
  loading: 'Loading history…',
  systemActor: 'the system',
  unknownVerb: '{actor} performed {verb}.',
  sentences: {
    'ticket.status':   '{actor} moved this from {fromStatus} to {toStatus}.',
    'ticket.assign':   '{actor} assigned this to {toAssignee}.',
    'ticket.unassign': '{actor} unassigned this from {fromAssignee}.',
    'ticket.category': '{actor} changed the category from {fromCategory} to {toCategory}.',
    'ticket.priority': '{actor} changed the priority from {fromPriority} to {toPriority}.',
    'ticket.reply':    '{actor} replied.',
    'ticket.create':   '{actor} raised this ticket.',
    'ticket.resolve':  '{actor} resolved this ticket.',
  },
},
```

Ar equivalents translate the whole sentence, not fragments — the placeholder order in each Arabic template can differ from English.

Add to `t.errors` (both files) the three domain codes the API now names (confirm exact codes against the CRM-83 plan; likely `ticket_not_found`, `history_forbidden`, `history_unavailable`). Never compose an error sentence from `fields`.

Wording constraint: nothing in these keys, nor in any commit message or code comment introduced by this story, may mention AI assistance.

### 4 — Screen: `TicketHistory`

Create file: `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketHistory.tsx`

- Props: `{ ticketId: string }`.
- Composition (shared primitives only):
  - `Card` wrapping a `Stack` of `Heading` (`t.tickets.history.heading`), the list, and the "Load more" `Button`.
  - `status === 'loading'` on first load → `Skeleton` rows (match the count/height used in `TicketQueuePage.tsx`).
  - `status === 'error'` → `ErrorState` with `t.errors[error.code] ?? t.errors.unknown`.
  - `status === 'success' && items.length === 0` → `EmptyState` with `t.tickets.history.emptyTitle` / `emptyBody` (D-2).
  - `status === 'success' && items.length > 0` → an ordered `<ol>` of `<li>` entries, each rendering:
    - The sentence returned by `formatHistorySentence(entry, t, formatValue)`.
    - A localised timestamp via `useFormatters().formatDateTime(entry.at)` (BR-3). Do not call `toLocaleString` inline.
  - When `nextCursor` is not null, render `Button` labelled `t.tickets.history.loadMore` that calls `loadMore()`.
- Order preservation: render items in the exact order the API returned them; do not sort client-side.
- **No literal text in JSX**, including no separator glyphs typed between tags. Any punctuation goes inside a translated string.
- Value formatter: implement `formatValue(field, value)` locally on the page (or export from `history-sentence.ts`) that maps e.g. `field === 'status' ? t.tickets.status[value] : value`.

### 5 — Mount the region on the ticket detail area

File: `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` (or the ticket detail view CRM-83's frontend companion mounts) — locate where a single ticket is rendered and slot in `<TicketHistory ticketId={ticket.id} />` beneath the resolve/assign controls. If no ticket-detail view exists yet, expose `TicketHistory` from `web/src/pages/tickets/index.ts` (create if missing) so the next story can drop it in without a rewrite.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty history** — API returns `{ items: [], nextCursor: null }`. Render `EmptyState` with `t.tickets.history.emptyTitle` and `emptyBody`. Enforced in `TicketHistory.tsx` in the `items.length === 0` branch.
- **Null actor** — `entry.actor === null` when the system acted. Sentence substitutes `t.tickets.history.systemActor`. Enforced in `formatHistorySentence` in `web/src/shared/i18n/history-sentence.ts`. Do not invent a name.
- **Unknown verb** — the API returns a verb the resource file does not know. Sentence falls through to `t.tickets.history.unknownVerb` filled with `{verb}` and `{actor}`. Legible, no crash, no blank line.
- **Missing slot value** — a placeholder appears in the template but the corresponding key is absent from `before`/`after`. Substitute the empty string and log nothing; the sentence must still render.
- **Localised timestamp** — never render `entry.at` verbatim. `useFormatters().formatDateTime` produces the reader's locale (BR-3).
- **Arabic word order** — verified by having each sentence be a whole per-language template with placeholders; concatenation is not used.
- **Cursor exhaustion** — `nextCursor === null` hides the "Load more" button.
- **Concurrent "Load more"** — `useRequest` prevents overlapping calls; the button is disabled while `status === 'loading'`.
- **API error** — `t.errors[code]` renders inside `ErrorState`; never compose from `fields`. Unknown code falls back to `t.errors.unknown`.
- **Double URL prefix** — writing `/api/v1/tickets/...` yields `/api/v1/api/v1/...` (CRM-72's test caught this). Enforced by using `request()` which already prefixes.

## Test Plan

All tests use Vitest + Testing Library; the web suite does not typecheck via `npm test`. Run `npm run build` from `web/` to catch type errors.

1. **`web/src/shared/i18n/history-sentence.test.ts`** (unit)
   - `formatHistorySentence` substitutes placeholders for a known verb (`ticket.status`) using English resources.
   - Same input with Arabic resources produces the Arabic template (different word order preserved).
   - Null actor substitutes `t.tickets.history.systemActor`.
   - Unknown verb falls back to `t.tickets.history.unknownVerb`.
   - Missing slot value substitutes empty string, does not throw.
   - Status/category values are looked up in `t.tickets.status.*` / `t.tickets.categories.*`, not returned raw.

2. **`web/src/pages/tickets/TicketHistory.test.tsx`** (integration)
   - Renders `Skeleton` while loading.
   - Renders `EmptyState` with the `emptyTitle` string when `items` is empty (D-2).
   - Renders one `<li>` per entry, in the exact order returned by the API.
   - Renders a localised timestamp (assert against a formatter output, not a raw ISO string) (BR-3).
   - Renders the sentence built from the resource file, not the verb (`ticket.status` never appears in the DOM) (BR-6).
   - Shows "Load more" only when `nextCursor !== null`; clicking it triggers another fetch with the returned cursor (BR-4).
   - Hides "Load more" when `nextCursor === null`.
   - Error branch renders `t.errors[code]`.
   - Uses a **fresh `Response` per fetch call** in the stub (L-30) — a body is read-once; symptom of getting this wrong is a timing-out test, not a body error.

3. **`web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts`** — already exists; verify it still passes with the new keys added to both `en.ts` and `ar.ts`.

4. **`web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`** — already exists; verify it still passes. No literal text or separator glyphs in `TicketHistory.tsx`.

5. **Language switch smoke** — extend or add a case in an existing switching test (see `web/src/shared/i18n/language-switch.test.tsx`) to assert the history heading changes when the locale toggles.

Match the fetch-stubbing style of `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.test.tsx` and `web/src/pages/customers/CustomersPage.test.tsx`.

## Review note — what this plan got wrong

The plan was written without reading the route it consumes. Six of its
statements about the API are inventions, and each one is recorded here because
a plan is read later by somebody with no way to tell which of its facts were
checked.

1. **There is no `nextCursor`.** `GET /tickets/:id/history` answers
   `{ items, total, limit, offset }` — offset paging, like every list in this
   API (`api/src/features/tickets/tickets.service.js`, `history`). The plan
   built a type, a hook signature, two edge cases and a Done Criteria box on a
   cursor that does not exist. The screen reads "is there more" from
   `entries.length < total` and asks for the next window by offset.

2. **`actor` is not an object.** The route returns `actorId: string | null`.
   Names are resolved on the client from the staff list, which is the precedent
   CRM-61 set for note authors and CRM-72 set for assignees — the API answers
   with ids, and the screen that needs names is the one already holding the
   list.

3. **The verbs were guessed.** The plan wrote sentences for eight, five of
   which nothing emits. The API writes three: `ticket.create`, `ticket.assign`
   and `ticket.status`. Sentences exist for those three and no others; the
   unknown-verb line is the mechanism by which a fourth arrives legibly, which
   is what the plan got right.

4. **An assignment is one verb and three sentences.** What happened is in the
   diff, not in the name — given to somebody, taken off somebody, or moved
   between two people. Read off `before`/`after` rather than asking the API for
   three verbs to save a branch here.

5. **`t.errors.unknown` and three new domain codes do not exist.** The
   catalogue is frozen and UPPER_SNAKE (`web/src/shared/api/errors.ts`); the
   fallback every other screen uses is `t.errors.INTERNAL`. The history route
   throws `NOT_FOUND` and nothing else. No error key was added.

6. **`formatDateTime` and `t.tickets.status.*` do not exist.** The formatter is
   `formatDate(value, options)`; the status words are `statusLabel()` in
   `web/src/pages/tickets/ticket-labels.ts`, which CRM-58 extracted so two
   screens could not disagree. A third copy here would have been that defect
   again.

7. **Where it mounts.** The plan offered "expose it from an index so the next
   story can drop it in" as a fallback, which ships a component nothing
   renders. There is no ticket detail screen; the queue row is where a ticket
   is shown and where its assign and status controls already are, so the trail
   sits under them behind a disclosure, closed, fetched on opening. A row that
   read its own history on mount would make one page of the queue twenty-five
   requests, and a test pins that it does not.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for confirmation before proceeding to the next story.**
